title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's standard processes and best practices for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance & feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new people managers.

Scope
Applies to all full-time employees, contractors converting to full-time, and hiring managers across engineering, product, research, and go-to-market teams. Exceptions (legal/regulatory hires, government contracts) are documented in related pages.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

Short intro
Our hiring process is designed to be inclusive, efficient, and evidence-based: candidates are assessed against a role-specific scorecard and a consistent interview loop to reduce bias and hire for mission-critical outcomes. Strive for a time-to-offer under 30 calendar days for most roles.

High-level steps
- Role definition & scorecard: hiring manager drafts the role description and a 3-5 item scorecard (core responsibilities + success metrics). People Ops reviews leveling and compensation band.
- Sourcing & outreach: internal referral, pipeline outreach, and posted requisition. Track source in the ATS.
- Phone screen (recruiter): confirm interest, logistics, compensation band, work authorization, candidate experience expectations.
- Technical/functional interviews: 2-3 interviews focusing on the scorecard dimensions (work sample, system design, coding, customer & product sense as relevant).
- Behavioral interview: culture fit and leadership principles, using structured STAR-based questions.
- Hiring decision & calibration: interviewers submit scorecards within 48 hours; hiring manager convenes panel for pass/fail and calibration.
- Offer & negotiation: People Ops prepares compensation package and sends offer. Target acceptance rate > 70% and time-to-offer < 3 business days from decision.
- Reference checks & background: performed after verbal offer and before finalization for roles requiring vetting.

Interview loop guidance
- Use the published scorecard for the role and align questions to 2-3 measurable outcomes.
- No more than 6 interviews in the loop unless exceptional circumstances.
- All interviewers must complete unconscious bias training annually.
- Document candidate feedback in the ATS within 48 hours and give constructive feedback when requested.

Responsibilities
- Hiring manager: owns scorecard, interview rubric, final hiring decision, onboarding plan, and ramp goals.
- Recruiter: manages pipeline, coordinates interviews, candidate experience, and offers.
- People Ops: provides compensation guidance, equity and benefits counseling, and final offer execution.

Metrics & targets
- Time-to-offer (target): <= 30 calendar days from requisition approval to offer delivered.
- Offer acceptance rate (target): >= 70% rolling 90-day.
- Candidate NPS (target): >= 60.

2) New hire onboarding (preboarding -> 90 days)

Pre-boarding (1-7 days before start)
- People Ops sends welcome packet with offer letter, benefits overview, first-week agenda, and required forms.
- IT ticket created for account provisioning, hardware shipment, and access requests.
- Hiring manager prepares Day 1 schedule and introduces the buddy.

Day 1 checklist
- Welcome & orientation (People Ops): benefits enrollment, company values, security training.
- Manager meeting: role expectations, immediate priorities, 30/60/90 plan.
- Team welcome: introductions, team rituals, core tools overview.
- Workspace & access verification: email, Slack, CI/CD, Jira, internal wikis.

First 30 / 60 / 90 plan (manager + new hire)
- 0-30 days: learning the codebase/product, completing required trainings, small initial deliverable with a peer reviewer.
- 30-60 days: own a small project, contribute to team discussions, and present a summary of learnings.
- 60-90 days: deliver on the first scoped project, demonstrate competency on scorecard items, and plan for next quarter's goals.

Onboarding checklist (table format expressed in text)
- Accounts & Access: [Slack, Google Workspace, Okta, Jira, Confluence, CI/CD] - expected provisioned by Day 1.
- Hardware: MacBook/approved laptop, peripherals, VPN config - shipped 3 business days pre-start.
- Mandatory trainings: Security (1 day), Data Handling (3 days), Code of Conduct (1 day).
- Team onboarding: schedule 1:1s with cross-functional partners within first 2 weeks.

Buddy program & manager responsibilities
- Assign a buddy for first 30 days (peer-level) to support day-to-day questions and social onboarding.
- Manager must schedule weekly 1:1s for first 90 days and provide explicit feedback after 30 and 60 days.

3) Performance & feedback cycles

Principles
- Feedback should be frequent, specific, and tied to outcomes on the scorecard. Managers own performance development; People Ops facilitates calibration and process integrity.

Cycle cadence
- Continuous feedback: use Slack/1:1s for immediate coaching and recognition.
- Quarterly check-ins: lightweight written update + manager conversation focused on goals and blockers.
- Annual review: formal written review, calibration meeting, and compensation adjustments.

Process details
- Goal setting: managers and reports set quarterly goals aligned to team objectives and company themes. Use quantitative success metrics where possible.
- Check-in template: current priorities, successes, blockers, learning goals, and support requested.
- Ratings & calibration: managers submit draft ratings to People Ops; calibration groups review cross-team distribution to ensure consistency.
- Promotion & leveling: promotion packets include impact examples, peer feedback, manager endorsement, and proposed new responsibilities. People Ops coordinates the final level decision.

Underperformance & PIP
- Coaching first: document expectations, set 30-60 day improvement goals, and provide resources.
- Formal PIP: when coaching does not lead to expected improvement, use a 60-90 day PIP with clear success criteria, weekly check-ins, and a single owner for reviews. People Ops must be engaged before a PIP is issued.

4) Manager playbook (practical guidance)

Hiring & interviewing
- Create a role-specific scorecard before posting the role. Define the top 3 outcomes you expect within 6 months.
- Panel interviewers should assess disjoint areas of the scorecard to avoid duplicated evaluation.

One-on-ones & cadence
- Weekly 1:1s are minimum during ramp. Use a shared agenda and track action items in Confluence.
- Quarterly skip-levels: schedule at least one skip-level per quarter to collect upward feedback.

Feedback & recognition
- Give feedback in the moment and document it in the employee's private performance notes (manager-owned).
- Use public recognition for cross-team impact and written feedback for promotion packets.

Career development & promotions
- Work with each direct report to build a 12-month development plan including stretch projects and learning commitments.
- For promotion, compile a packet that includes 3-5 concrete impact examples mapped to the next level's rubric.

Legal & compliance checkpoints
- For hires in regulated roles or locations (e.g., positions with data residency or government contracting constraints), consult Security & Legal teams before final offer.
- Background check and right-to-work verification must be completed where required by law.

5) Policies & special cases

Remote hiring & relocation
- Hiring is remote-friendly. If relocation is requested or required, People Ops will evaluate relocation package and timeline during offer stage.

Contractors & staffing conversions
- Contractors converting to full-time follow a simplified interview loop (target: 2 interviews + manager discussion) but must have a scorecard and calibration.

Confidential or sensitive hires
- For hires involving classified or customer-sensitive projects, label the requisition as restricted and engage Security and Legal for additional vetting.

Appendices

Appendix A - Sample scorecard (example text)
Role: Senior Backend Engineer - Outcomes (top 3): 1) Deliver reliable streaming ingestion pipeline; 2) Reduce tail latency by 20% for high-throughput endpoints; 3) Mentor two engineers to independent ownership.

Appendix B - Offer checklist (items to verify before sending offer)
1) Compensation band & equity approval documented
2) Manager sign-off on budget and start date
3) Background check requirements assessed
4) Initial 30/60/90 plan drafted
5) Hardware & access orders placed

Appendix C - Manager 30/60/90 feedback template (text)
- 30-day: Initial ramp assessment, knowledge gaps, early wins.
- 60-day: Progress on first project, collaboration and communication.
- 90-day: Project delivery, independent impact, recommendation for next quarter goals.
